clue.text: Divine, the French crew's accommodation

parts.note: to divine is to predict or foretell, i.e. forecast
le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A clergyman and a French crew share their living quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like a noun (a clergyman) but is the verb meaning to foretell.
explanation.definitionFit: The forecastle is the forward part of a ship where sailors traditionally had their quarters.

clue.text: No end neglected — has to give up

indicators.note: No end means the final letter is removed

parts.note: forgot means failed to attend to, i.e. neglected

explanation.surface: Someone who neglects everything has to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' just links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo is to go without or relinquish something.

clue.text: Bat has always one to charge for protection

parts.note: a racket is a bat used in tennis or squash
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A bat always has someone to charge for protecting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs extortion schemes, including demanding money from businesses for so-called security.

clue.text: It lights obscure channel entries

indicators.note: obscure suggests the letters are muddled and their order hidden

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A lamp shines on hard-to-see entrances to a channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' looks like an adjective about the entries but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese lantern is a collapsible paper lamp, so something giving light.

clue.text: Trickery of the French in a sense

indicators.note: in means the French article goes inside the word for a sense

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses
le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: French trickery is apparent in a certain sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means deceptive dexterity, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Heroic lover — look around and find him

indicators.note: around means the word for look surrounds the next word

parts.note: to leer is to look slyly or lasciviously

explanation.surface: Look around for a heroic lover and you'll find him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heroic' means 'of Hero': in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover Hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Leander was the lover of Hero in Greek legend, drowning while swimming to her.

clue.text: Manages to hit back and bring down

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for hit from right to left

parts.note: to pot is to hit a ball into a pocket in snooker or billiards

explanation.surface: Someone manages to retaliate and floor an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns POTS into STOP; 'Manages to' merely links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing, to stop an opponent is to knock them down and out of the fight.

clue.text: The one to right of them

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: The one positioned to the right of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is the possessive form meaning belonging to those people.

clue.text: A rope sling — the standard fastening

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a buckle is a clasp for fastening a strap

explanation.surface: A rope sling secured with the usual clasp.
explanation.definitionFit: A parbuckle is a rope loop used to raise or lower cylindrical objects like barrels.

clue.text: Remnants in bedding

parts.note: a bed cover made by stitching together leftover scraps of fabric

explanation.definitionFit: A patchwork quilt is a bedcover sewn from many odd pieces of cloth.

clue.text: Get the message about the church? I have!

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning concerning or about
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you've heard the news about the church, and says they have.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a message is to take it in when it is delivered, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: A husband? You are, they say, a lover

parts.note: a mate is a spouse or partner, so a husband

indicators.note: they say signals that the next words are taken as they are pronounced

parts.note: spoken aloud, 'you are' sounds like the letters U and R

explanation.surface: Someone tells a husband he is a romantic lover.
explanation.walkthrough: An amateur, from Latin amator, is literally one who does something for love.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur is literally a lover of an activity, from the Latin for one who loves.

clue.text: Silver was on edge, worried about set-back

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled letters surround the next piece
worried suggests the letters of 'on edge' are shaken about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: back, in 'set-back', says the word for set is read in reverse

parts.note: a jelly or hair product sets, and gel means to set

explanation.surface: Someone called Silver was nervous about a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' scrambles ON EDGE into ONE GED, and 'about' places LEG (GEL turned round by 'back') in the middle. Long John Silver in Treasure Island has one leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver, the pirate of Treasure Island, famously had only a single leg and a crutch.

clue.text: In copper change for islanders here

indicators.note: In tells us the following anagram goes inside the symbol for copper

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: change says the letters of 'for' are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone changes copper coins for local islanders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' turns FOR into ORF, placed inside CU. 'copper' looks like coins but is the chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea, so it is where those islanders live.

clue.text: Long note comes back in reverberation

indicators.note: comes back means the concealed letters run from right to left
in signals that the letters sit inside the word reverberation

explanation.surface: A long musical note echoes back in the reverberation.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside reVERBeration lies EVERB, which 'comes back' to read BREVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a musical note lasting twice as long as a semibreve, the longest in common use.

clue.text: Pull up in seconds in reverse

indicators.note: in means the reversed word is placed inside the word for seconds

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it, so seconds means backs

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: Someone pulls up within seconds by reversing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like time but is the verb meaning supports, BACKS; 'up' turns DRAW into WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Backwards means in the opposite direction, toward the rear.

clue.text: Atavistic way to treat small fish?

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned angler's approach to an undersized catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Atavistic means reverting to an ancestral type, and an undersized catch is returned to the water.

clue.text: Brandy and beer a boy swallows very quietly

indicators.note: swallows means the word for beer takes in the next piece

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
pp (pianissimo) is the musical direction for very quietly
Jack is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy quietly downs brandy and beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints APPLETACK, an OCR slip: the wordplay gives JACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Applejack is an American spirit distilled from cider, a kind of apple liquor.

clue.text: Break a record in flavour

indicators.note: Break suggests the words are smashed and their letters reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An athlete breaks a record while in good form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break a record' sounds like a sporting achievement but signals an anagram of A RECORD IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriander is an herb whose leaves and seeds are used to add taste to food.

clue.text: Porter invests gold in party piece

indicators.note: invests means the word for gold is put within the other pieces

parts.note: a do is a party or social event
a man is a piece in chess or draughts
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A porter puts money into his party piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party piece' reads as a show-off act but splits into DO and MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorman is a building's attendant, also called a porter.

clue.text: Climbing fruit-tree I dropped, falling back

indicators.note: Climbing in a down clue means the letters are read upwards
dropped means the letter I is removed

parts.note: an espalier is a fruit tree trained flat against a wall

explanation.surface: Someone climbing a fruit tree dropped and fell back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes I from ESPALIER to leave ESPALER, which 'Climbing' turns into RELAPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a slide back into an earlier worse state, such as illness.

clue.text: Regret holding gym lessons for money

indicators.note: holding means the first word contains the second

parts.note: to rue is to regret
PE stands for physical education, school gym lessons

explanation.surface: Someone regrets paying for gym classes.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India and several other countries.

clue.text: Quiet game

explanation.surface: A hushed game.
explanation.definitionFit: Whist is an old exclamation meaning hush, and also a card game for four players.

clue.text: The child is a girl

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone announces that the baby is a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, so a child or children.

clue.text: Indirectly, I quell boy's revolt

indicators.note: revolt suggests the letters rise up and are overturned into a new order

parts.note: the letters of I, quell and boy, with the possessive adding none

explanation.surface: Someone claims to put down a boy's rebellion in a roundabout way.
explanation.definitionFit: Obliquely means at a slant, so not in a direct or straightforward manner.

clue.text: They're played with by most of you repeatedly on Sunday

indicators.note: repeatedly means the shortened word appears twice
most of means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Most of you play with these toys over and over on Sundays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Yo-yos are spinning toys on a string that are flicked up and down.

clue.text: Somewhere to speak or possibly play badly

indicators.note: possibly hints that the two letters of 'or' could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
to strum is to play a stringed instrument casually or unskilfully

explanation.surface: A speaker's platform, or perhaps a poor performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges OR into RO, before STRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform from which a speaker addresses an audience.

clue.text: Chief Muslim title held in reversion by peer

indicators.note: held means one piece is contained within the other

parts.note: to peer is to look closely, to pry

indicators.note: in reversion says the title is turned back to front

parts.note: an amir (emir) is a title of a Muslim ruler or commander

explanation.surface: A peer holds a Muslim noble title that will revert to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' looks like a noble but is the verb to look; 'in reversion' turns AMIR into RIMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Primary means first or principal, a synonym for main or foremost.

clue.text: Twist what Cain did

explanation.surface: A Biblical turn of events.
explanation.definitionFit: To slew is to swing round or veer, and Cain slew (killed) his brother Abel in Genesis.

clue.text: Dukes aren't given to breaking promises

indicators.note: breaking suggests the words are broken up and their letters reassembled

parts.note: the letters of the two words, the apostrophe giving none

explanation.surface: Aristocrats are said not to break their word.
explanation.definitionFit: To undertake is to pledge or commit to doing something.
